$comment: Every loader that reads versions runs these, with the same upgrade written in its own language: v1's `retries` becomes v2's `retry.attempts`. `reads` is what the binary declares: `both` is N=2 with N-1=1 and an upgrade, `current` is N=2 alone, `load` is the plain loader (which reads v1 only) given `schema`. `upgrade` replaces the good upgrade with one that drops `retry` (`drops-retry`) or fails (`fails`). `want` maps a dotted path to the value the loaded document holds there; `refused` lists what the error must contain. No error may contain a value from the file but the version.

cases.name: the current version loads as it is
the previous version is validated as itself, then upgraded
no apiVersion is v1, and is upgraded
a newer version is refused, not read as the current one
refused: apiVersion: v3 is newer than this binary reads (v2, v1)

cases.name: another kind of document is refused
refused: apiVersion: names another kind of document; this binary reads example.com/notifier

cases.name: a version that is not of the form is refused by its form
a v1 document is validated against v1, never guessed at
refused: retry: not a key this service reads

cases.name: a binary that reads only v2 refuses v1
refused: apiVersion: v1 is older than this binary reads (v2)

cases.name: a binary that reads only v2 refuses a document with no version
refused: apiVersion: absent, which is v1, older than this binary reads (v2)

cases.name: an upgrade that produces an invalid document is refused, and says it was upgraded
an upgrade that fails is refused, naming both versions
the plain loader refuses any version but v1
refused: apiVersion: v2 is newer than this binary reads (v1)
